name: APP-1 to APP-4: missing stays missing
summary: Missing inputs propagate and never read as zero; the cash identity; the least funding gap; status never upgrades. Each proved in Agda, Rocq and Lean.

name: Atlas views
summary: The catalogue and the A to Z and organisation views, generated from the census rows and checked for staleness by `just check-views`.

counsel.engineering: Removes the hand-copying of statements that every re-proof does today.

name: Bridges by construction
summary: Generate the Agda, Rocq and Lean forms of a statement from one source (Q-2.3, E-2.3), so a re-proof starts from a statement known to match.

name: Bridge candidates
summary: Three unassessed candidate links between theorems in different repositories and provers (tropical MaxPlus, resource-algebra M-2, squeakwell). Candidates, not evidence.

counsel.cartographer: The first real convergence between repositories; everything cross-repo waits on it.

name: Bridge lock pilot
summary: The full bridge record for two pilots, a squeakwell ladder row and resource-algebra to tropical-types (WO 5.2, ruling D-7 a): what is claimed equal, by which map, checked how.

name: Census of the estate
summary: The proof census of 465 public repositories: 249 rows of proof files, holes and axioms, each at a pinned commit and time.

name: Census on a schedule
summary: A scheduled census workflow as the one writer of the census rows (WO 5.3), so refreshes stop arriving by hand and unrecorded.

name: Centre computations
summary: Over locked bridges: classes under a criterion, their order, contradictions, and the five different absences (RA 786-801).

counsel.maths: The deepest open question on the board; it decides what S-1 even says.
counsel.science: Pre-register what result means A, B or C before computing.

name: Is a chain enough? (X-PF1)
summary: Decide whether proof status is a chain or needs a lattice: outcomes A, B or C, with a seven-value free distributive lattice as the candidate. Outcome C changes the standards canon.

name: CI records its own runs
summary: A trusted publisher that writes each green run's ledger rows to the repository, so no human copies rows. The piece standards PR 1675 leaves open.

name: Claims registry
summary: Pins 53 claims in their home repositories and derives each grade from the home receipt with the pinned canon reader. No grade is typed.

name: Cohort model in Agda
summary: The cohort-economics model of the applied shelf, with three number modes and synthetic examples generated into Agda from JSON Lines.

name: Concept commons
summary: The horizon of the atlas (M4): a commons of the estate's concepts, navigable by A to Z, subject (MSC2020), project and provenance.

name: Propose and dispose corpus
summary: A corpus as a view over bridges and receipts (E-H.1), and 20 ungraded Agda theorems given model-proposed Rocq and Lean legs, kept BRIDGE-PENDING until checked (E-H.2).

blocked_by: Agda2Dedukti fails on a parameterised record in Set1 and rejects --cubical-compatible; Lambdapi raw_lean and raw_coq drop rewrite rules. A transport row stays a re-proof until a fixed release passes the round trip.

counsel.contrarian: Policy puts this route first, yet every re-proof so far went the other way.

name: Transport through Dedukti
summary: Check an Agda proof in Rocq and Lean by translating it through Dedukti and Lambdapi instead of re-proving it, the route PROOF-POLICY section 2 puts first.

counsel.contrarian: Cheapest node on the board, and the auditor's favourite.
counsel.soundness: Every one of these is a claim with no receipt behind it; mend before adding.

name: Mend the status documents
summary: ROADMAP, PROOF-NEEDS, README and the intend contract contradict the receipts (PWG-1 vs PWG-2ii, receipts called planned that exist, stage states). Make each agree with the derived facts.

name: Theorem dossier
summary: The eight-item dossier for each theorem (Line 0), scored first on THY-1, five januskey theorems and two each of secret-types and lintel (E-0). Its home (here or standards, R-5) is still open.

name: Echo mirror records
summary: Bridge records for the six languages that mirror echo-types (E-2.5), with the graded-comonad disagreement kept as an open question.

counsel.publications: Nobody has this list; it is citable on its own.
counsel.science: Each entry should come with a counterexample that shows it.

name: Closed list of encoding differences
summary: A closed, tested list of the ways the same statement differs between Agda, Rocq and Lean (Q-2.1), built from the existing comparisons as bridge records (E-2.1).

name: PWG-2ii across the estate
summary: The long horizon (Q-H.3): the 900 and more ungraded theorems of the estate each carry two checked recheck legs. The question is whether that takes months or years.

counsel.economics: A few hours of filing could unblock a whole route for everyone.

name: File the transport reproducers
summary: File the THY-1 reproducers upstream (E-2.4): the Agda2Dedukti crash and option gaps, and Lambdapi dropping rules. Filing is the owner's act.

counsel.economics: The first output a business reader would recognise.

name: Thirteen-week forecast
summary: A synthetic thirteen-week cash forecast on the proved cohort model (E-4.1), the first worked decision of the applied shelf.

blocked_by: the estate coordinator's answer on how GELS panels take their data (asked 2026-11-24); no feed is written until a reader is agreed
name: Maths panel in GELS
summary: A panel in GELS, the estate display, for the maths: the frontier of this tree, the grade census with its denominator, and the open decisions.

name: Generated Idris2 token laws
summary: Generate the Idris2 token laws of the proof-route Token module from S-1 (E-3.2), so the engineering side cites the theorem instead of restating it.

name: Theorem to code: januskey
summary: Follow one theorem into running code (E-3.1): the januskey slice T-1, with T-10 open and G-2 assumed, and a composite status for the whole (Q-3.1).

name: Liquidity shelf
summary: The liquidity part of the applied shelf: a forecast whose every verdict carries its proof status, from synthetic data only.

name: Paper: receipts, not claims
summary: A methods paper: proof status derived from machine receipts, graded by witness count, never typed, with the registry as a working instance across an estate.

name: Paper: an algebra of proof status
summary: S-1 to S-3 written up: proof status as a dioid, its monotone evaluation, and the grade as a checked function of the receipt.

counsel.publications: A complete, small, checked result: the easiest first paper.

name: Note: feature reachability
summary: A short note on THY-1: why requesting every feature is a sound check for absence, with the three-prover receipt as artefact. Its dependant is a real standards rule.

counsel.soundness: The only road back to PWG-1 for THY-1 and APP-1 to APP-4.

name: Proof lanes in a pinned image
summary: Run the three proof lanes in a container image pinned by digest, the condition PROOF-POLICY now sets for PWG-1 (standards#1625). The Guix shell alone does not qualify.

name: Proof gate in pinned Guix
summary: Agda 2.7.0.1, Rocq 8.18.0 and Lean 4.29.0 check every gated module on every commit, with an axiom audit over theorems and definitions and planted controls that must fail.

counsel.publications: Everything else here is invisible until this happens.
counsel.soundness: Publish only views whose checks are green, or the site states what the receipts do not.

name: Publish the atlas
summary: Deploy the built site (WO 4.3). The hold ran to 2026-11-24; deploying is outward-facing, so it waits for a fresh owner question first.

name: Back to PWG-1
summary: THY-1 and APP-1 to APP-4 derive PWG-1 again, from receipts whose rows name the pinned image.

counsel.engineering: One generator for the estate instead of one per repository.

name: Shared receipt generator
summary: Adopt the standards generator: the receipt is generated from a run ledger, and the gate lists each green run's ledger rows. Pull request 122.

name: Proof receipts
summary: The PROOF-POLICY 8.5.1 receipt of Mathesis: per-leg run, commit, checker, inputs manifest and axioms, checked by the shared git checker and read by the canon reader.

counsel.cartographer: The registry is only as current as the home receipts.

name: Receipts campaign
summary: Home repositories re-record their receipts (WO 5.1): secret-types and lintel for the reader they fail, resource-algebra for its Lean leg. Takes 12 ungraded theorems towards a grade.

counsel.cartographer: Converge: the laws exist, at a grade, in their home repository.

name: S-1 by reuse of resource-algebra
summary: Prove only the morphism here, and take the dioid laws from resource-algebra's E-1 to E-3 (already PWG-2i) through a locked bridge, instead of proving them again.

counsel.contrarian: resource-algebra already pins E-1 to E-3; proving it again here may be duplication.
counsel.maths: A real algebra of evidence; the centre of the research programme.

name: S-1: tokens form a dioid
summary: The status tokens form a ResourceAlgebra and dioid with an annihilating zero, with an injective strict morphism into MinMax. Agda against resource-algebra at a pin, re-proved in Rocq and Lean (E-1.1).

name: S-2: evaluation is monotone
summary: Positive evaluation of status is monotone; proved once, with its home in Mathesis (R-3).

counsel.soundness: Turns the reader from trusted code into a checked one.

name: S-3: the grade is a function
summary: The Proof Witness Grade is a total monotone function of the receipt, and the canon reader agrees with it on every case, shown by exhaustion as in residual-evidence-types (E-1.3).

counsel.economics: A forecast that can say undecided is worth more than one that guesses.
counsel.teacher: Three-valued logic with money attached: an easy story to teach.

name: S-4 and S-5: honest cash verdicts
summary: A sound three-valued cash verdict over intervals, where missing means unbounded (S-4), and more uncertainty never strengthens a verdict (S-5). Reuses residual-evidence-types at a pin; pass is PWG-3 (E-4.2).

name: Atlas site (build)
summary: Renders every generated view with Asciidoctor and fails on any warning or broken link. It builds; it does not deploy.

counsel.science: Takes a statistical result that is only tested and makes it a theorem.

name: From oracle to theorem
summary: S-MN and S-DM (the multinomial logit closed form and the DM contrast limit) are tested only, against MetaManifold-WebUI as oracle. Prove them in Agda, Rocq and Lean for admission (Q-2.6).

name: Talk: an atlas of an estate
summary: A talk on mapping the mathematics of hundreds of repositories, with every status traced to a receipt.

counsel.teacher: Shows why a proof matters to someone who reads spreadsheets, not theorems.

name: Cohort economics, taught
summary: A worked tutorial: a small business model where missing data stays missing, with the proofs alongside and synthetic data only.

name: Theory shelf and ledger
summary: The admission rule for theory no single system owns, with an append-only ledger of every grade and receipt change. One theorem admitted so far.

name: THY-1: reachability is monotone
summary: In a dependency graph with feature-guarded edges, a node unreachable with every feature requested is unreachable under any request. Proved in Agda, re-proved in Rocq and Lean.

counsel.cartographer: The ruling lands in standards PROOF-POLICY, not here; carry it there.
counsel.maths: A theorem about an order is only as good as the order; settle it first.

name: Settle the order of status tokens
summary: The research programme rules open < argued < tested-only < proven-with-postulates < proven (R-1), but resource-algebra E-1 states tested-only < argued, and both cite PROOF-POLICY section 5. One order must win before the token algebra is proved.

name: The ultraplan
summary: This tech tree: data first, with derived eras, frontier, forks, confluences and advisor picks, and a done that must show evidence.

name: Value of information
summary: Decision science on the shelf: what a missing input is worth to know, computed from the three-valued verdicts. No optimiser (decision-science README).

name: What is owed
summary: A view of the standards requirements master list beside the census and the registry (WO 5.4): what each repository owes, and what it has.
